title: Learning as a family
hookLine: a question at dinner, a story at bedtime
tomorrow: a younger cousin asks Noa to teach him. what does she even know?

lines: A ROAST CHICKEN AND TRAFFIC TALK.
cards: Friday night at Noa's: her mom Rachel, Saba David, a roast chicken, and the usual talk about traffic. Pirkei Avot has a test for a table like that.
If three eat at one table and say no words of Torah over it, it's as if they ate offerings to the dead. If three eat at one table and do say words of Torah, it's as if they ate at God's own table.
So it isn't the food that does it. It's a few words worth saying.

teach.h: IN THE HOUSE, AND ON THE WAY.
teach.b: Learning as a family doesn't need a curriculum. Deuteronomy puts the teaching right inside the house: "when thou sittest in thy house, and when thou walkest by the way." At the table, in the car, at bedtime.
One question can do it: what would you have done in today's story? What's something about our family you've never asked? For a parent who isn't sure what to teach, that's a sentence to start with.

teach.h: A WEEK OF LEARNING FOR LIFE.
teach.b: Now hold up the week. Akiva at the well, beside his son: choose next year's text. A sword against studying alone: learn in pairs.
The Torah read around again: the cycle never ends. A page, or a line: any pace counts. Five words lighting up a page: more hebrew.
Two chairs and the Presence: learn together.

teach.h: A TABLE WITH A QUESTION ON IT.
teach.b: And now a family table with one question on it.
Something to tell a friend tonight: Pirkei Avot says a meal with a few words of Torah is like eating at God's table.

how: Some Jewish families share words of Torah at the Shabbat table, a question about the week's portion or a story, and tell stories at bedtime, following Deuteronomy's 'when thou sittest in thy house'.

games.q: what does “learning as a family” mean?
o: a class parents take before a child's bar mitzvah
a family tree traced back through old records
a question at dinner, a story at bedtime

games.q: a week of learning for life — tap the pairs.
p: the end and the beginning, one day
three who eat and say words of Torah

in Deuteronomy, teaching children happens at a desk, in formal lessons
when thou sittest in thy house, and when thou walkest by the way.

games.q: you and your partner grew up in different religions, and you're raising a child together. you're unsure what to teach at dinner. what fits today's idea?
o: start with one question at the table, and let the child ask too.
wait until the two of you agree on a full plan of lessons.
leave it to a school or a class; home is for meals.
games.why: Deuteronomy puts teaching in the house and on the way, and Pirkei Avot says a few words over a meal change the table. one question is a start.

practice: Close your eyes and remember a question you asked as a kid that nobody really answered. Let it sit with you a moment.
Then choose one question you could bring to a meal at home this week, with whoever is there, family by birth or by choice.

wordCard.voice: Learning as a family: a question at dinner, a story at bedtime, teaching that happens in the house and on the way.

orig.note: Hebrew: 'and thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children' (Deuteronomy 6:7).

carryVoice: Your line: family learning. One question at the table is enough to start. That's the week.

sources.ref: Mishnah Avot 3:3 (Rabbi Shimon: three who ate at one table without words of Torah, as if they ate offerings to the dead; with words of Torah, as if they ate from the table of God)
